The Yemeni Armed Forces include the Army , Navy , Air Force , Border Guards , and Strategic Reserve Forces , supported by local militias and tribal units.
Following the Houthi takeover of Sana’a, Saudi Arabia intervened militarily in March 2015 , leading a coalition to restore Hadi’s government.
Its geographical coordinates are 15°N, 48°E , and it shares borders with Saudi Arabia (1,307 km) and Oman (294 km) , with a 1,906 km coastline .
Despite its deep cultural heritage and abundant potential, modern Yemen has endured prolonged instability, conflict, and humanitarian crises since the unification of North and South Yemen in 1990.
The ideological divide between the YAR and PDRY led to decades of tension and conflict, culminating in the unification of the two states on 22 May 1990 , forming the Republic of Yemen .
Despite intermittent clashes, peace negotiations continued into 2025 , underscoring Yemen’s fragile yet ongoing transition.
Geography and Natural Environment Yemen spans 527,968 square kilometres , including the islands of Perim and the Socotra Archipelago .
Economy and Infrastructure Yemen’s economy has collapsed under the weight of conflict, corruption, and resource depletion .
Main trading partners are the UAE, India, Saudi Arabia, and Oman .
Defence, Security, and Conflict Landscape Yemen’s military landscape is fragmented among rival factions.
Society, Heritage, and Culture Yemen’s cultural identity reflects a unique blend of Arab, Islamic, and ancient South Arabian traditions .
Known for its ancient civilisation, distinctive architecture, and pivotal location controlling the Bab el-Mandeb Strait , Yemen has historically served as a crossroads for African and Asian trade.
Historical Background and Political Evolution The modern state of Yemen was formed through the merger of two historically and ideologically distinct entities.
In the north, the Kingdom of Yemen , later the Yemen Arab Republic (YAR) , gained independence from the Ottoman Empire in 1918 .
In the south, Aden , a British colony since 1839, evolved into the People’s Democratic Republic of Yemen (PDRY) following British withdrawal in 1967 and the adoption of a Marxist system in 1970 .
A brief civil war in 1994 , triggered by southern secessionist attempts, was crushed by northern forces loyal to President Ali Abdullah Saleh , who had ruled since 1978.
From 2004 , the Houthi insurgency in the northern province of Sa’dah challenged the central government.
Rooted in the Zaydi Shia revivalist movement , the Houthis (Ansarallah) accused the state of marginalisation.
The Arab Spring (2011) further destabilised Yemen.
The ensuing war devastated Yemen’s infrastructure and economy, producing one of the world’s gravest humanitarian crises.
The Southern Transitional Council (STC) emerged in the south, demanding autonomy and further complicating the conflict landscape.
The western mountains are among Arabia’s most fertile regions, supporting terraced agriculture.
Highest point: Jabal an Nabi Shuʿayb (3,666 m) Climate: Predominantly arid; temperate in the highlands and hot, humid along the coast.
Environmental threats include groundwater depletion , desertification , and overgrazing .
Conflict and economic collapse have displaced approximately 4.8 million people .
Political Structure and Governance Yemen’s governance combines Islamic (Sharia) principles , civil codes , and tribal customary law .

Economic indicators (2024): Growth: –2.3% (estimated) Unemployment: 17.1% (youth 32%) Inflation: ~29% (2022) Public debt: >80% of GDP Sectoral composition: Agriculture – 28.7% Industry – 25.4% Services – 41.8% Agriculture, employing most Yemenis, produces sorghum, coffee, mangoes, and qat (a mild stimulant crop).
Exports include gold, fish, and scrap metal , totalling under $400 million , while imports exceed $4 billion .
Iran is accused of supplying weapons and training to the Houthis, deepening regional rivalries.
The 2022 UN truce significantly reduced airstrikes and civilian casualties, though sporadic fighting persists along key frontlines in Marib , Taiz , and Hudaydah .
The national emblem , an eagle clutching a scroll inscribed “Republic of Yemen,” signifies sovereignty.
